annotation.title_clean: 49 U.S. Code § 44810 - Airport safety and airspace hazard mitigation and enforcement
annotation.title_en: 49 U.S. Code § 44810 - Airport safety and airspace hazard mitigation and enforcement
annotation.authors_or_issuer: United States Congress (via Cornell LII, U.S. Code)
named_instruments_referenced: Computer Fraud and Abuse Act of 1986
annotation.summary_en: US federal statute (49 USC 44810, enacted by the FAA Reauthorization Act 2018, amended through 2024) requiring the FAA to plan for certifying counter-UAS detection and mitigation systems at airports, test them at five airports, make them eligible for airport grants, and run a remote-identification enforcement pilot. The section expires on 30 September 2028.
key_provisions_or_claims: The FAA Administrator must develop a plan to certify or authorise UAS detection and mitigation technologies at airports
Systems must be tested and evaluated at 5 airports, including one top-10 airport by passenger boardings
Airport sponsors may apply for airport improvement grants to buy certified counter-UAS systems
Certain criminal statutes (CFAA, Wiretap Act, Pen/Trap) do not apply to authorised testing activities
Pilot program for remote detection and identification enforcement against noncompliant UAS operators, with annual reporting
